vuln_id: ARVO arvo:37687 / libgd gdImageColorTransparent previous-transparent index -1 write

project.name: libgd
project.commit_note: The exact staged vulnerable source inspected here is the bundled libgd checkout at `b214ab236acac1fb5cf84491894b544027bccba5`, not metadata commit `dceb29a6f5e8b0fb5e21d14c39013efcbb9203ee`. This staged tree still contains the same vulnerable logic fixed by metadata commit `ba14dec6efe9d87fe80fa1d7bd3d5b0583e1320e`: `src/gd.c` line 917 clears `im->alpha[im->transparent]` without first checking `im->transparent != -1`, and the saved Stage 01 stack matches this line map (`src/gd.c:917`, `src/gd_gif_in.c:328`, `src/gd_gif_in.c:186`).

classification.classification_note: UBSan reports an index-out-of-bounds on `int [256]`, but the faulting operation is a write through the palette-alpha lvalue `im->alpha[im->transparent]`. The attacker controls the new transparent index (`color = 0` on the witnessed path), while the negative subscript comes from the fresh-image sentinel `im->transparent == -1`.

bug_description.original: The vulnerability occurs because gdImageColorTransparent does not correctly handle the case when im->transparent is set to -1, which is the initial value indicating that no transparent color has been set. This results in undefined behavior due to an out-of-bounds write to im->alpha[im->transparent] in gd.c, specifically at line 922. The issue can be triggered by loading a GIF through gdImageCreateFromGifPtr, leading to a runtime error where index -1 is accessed in an array of size 256.
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is the exact 28-byte GIF89a blob `47 49 46 38 39 61 20 20 20 FF 20 20 20 21 F9 01 FF 00 2C 20 1E 20 20 20 00 20 00 20`. In `DoExtension()`, the malformed Graphic Control Extension `21 F9 01 FF 00` advertises block size `0x01`, so `GetDataBlock()` fills only `buf[0]` after `memset(buf, 0, 4)` and leaves `buf[1..3] == 0`; because the transparency flag bit in `buf[0]` is set, `*Transparent = buf[3]` stores `0`. The following image descriptor allocates a fresh palette `gdImage` whose initialization leaves `im->transparent = -1`. `gdImageCreateFromGifCtx()` then calls `gdImageColorTransparent(im, 0)`. In the palette branch, `gdImageColorTransparent()` checks only the incoming `color` range and not whether a previous transparent entry exists, so `im->alpha[im->transparent] = gdAlphaOpaque;` writes to `im->alpha[-1]`. Stage 01 reproduced `UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: runtime error: index -1 out of bounds for type 'int [256]'` at `src/gd.c:917:29`, with stack `gdImageColorTransparent -> gdImageCreateFromGifCtx -> gdImageCreateFromGifPtr`. The staged patch fixes the exact obligation by guarding the previous-entry clear with `if (im->transparent != -1)`.

source.description: First project-code read that materializes the witness's malformed Graphic Control Extension bytes into the local state later interpreted as a transparent palette index.
source.value_from: The exact staged witness contains Graphic Control Extension bytes `21 F9 01 FF 00`. Because line 385 zeroes `buf[4]` before this read and the block-size byte is `0x01`, `GetDataBlock()` copies only the single data byte `0xFF` into `buf[0]` and leaves `buf[1..3] == 0`.
source.note: This is the scored source rather than `LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput()` because the harness only forwards `Data, Size` to `gdImageCreateFromGifPtr()`. `DoExtension()` is where project code first turns the staged bytes into vulnerability-relevant parser state.

tainted_value_origin.description: This assignment materializes the pending transparent palette index later passed to `gdImageColorTransparent()`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: On the witnessed path, step 1 leaves `buf[0] == 0xFF` and `buf[3] == 0` in the zero-initialized 4-byte GCE buffer, so this statement stores `Transparent = 0`.

root_cause.description: Missing guard on the current palette-image transparent slot before clearing the previous transparent entry.
root_cause.note: On the witnessed call, `color == 0`, `im->trueColor == 0`, and the only palette-path guard is `color >= gdMaxColors`; nothing checks whether `im->transparent` is still the sentinel `-1`. The staged patch fixes this exact obligation by wrapping the write in `if (im->transparent != -1)`.

sink.description: UBSan crash site. The palette transparency setter clears the previous transparent entry with subscript `-1` and writes before the 256-element `alpha` array.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports `gd.c:917:2: runtime error: index -1 out of bounds for type 'int [256]'` in `gdImageColorTransparent`, and `reproduction_report.json` names the same stack `gdImageColorTransparent -> gdImageCreateFromGifCtx -> gdImageCreateFromGifPtr`.

parser_admitted.description: Reaching this branch proves the staged witness was accepted as a GIF far enough to parse the Graphic Control Extension, read an image descriptor, allocate `im`, and preserve a non-`-1` pending transparent index into the transparency setter call.

coarse_trace.summary: The GIF extension parser reads the malformed one-byte Graphic Control Extension block into a zeroed 4-byte buffer, so the transparency flag is set while the would-be transparent-color byte remains zero.
The next image descriptor in the same witness allocates a fresh 32x32 palette `gdImage`, and its initialization leaves `im->transparent = -1` because no previous transparent slot exists yet.
Because the pending `Transparent` value is `0`, the GIF loader still calls `gdImageColorTransparent(im, 0)` on that fresh image.

The palette-image transparency setter checks only the incoming `color` range and then blindly clears the previous transparent entry, so the fresh-image sentinel `im->transparent == -1` becomes the crashing `alpha[-1]` write recorded by UBSan.

fine_trace.note: Source. `DoExtension()` zero-initializes its 4-byte Graphic Control Extension buffer and then reads the first extension data block. On the staged witness, the GCE bytes are `21 f9 01 ff 00`, so the size byte `0x01` copies only `0xff` into `buf[0]` and leaves `buf[1..3] == 0`.
The low bit of `buf[0] == 0xff` marks transparency as present, so `DoExtension()` stores `buf[3] == 0` into `Transparent`. This is the palette index later passed to `gdImageColorTransparent()`.

After the extension is consumed, the next marker in the staged witness is `0x2c` (image separator), and the descriptor bytes decode `width = 0x0020`, `height = 0x0020`. This call therefore allocates the `gdImage *im` for the witness's 32x32 frame.

depends_on.via: fd cursor after the GCE block

fine_trace.note: Initialization of the new `gdImage` seeds the vulnerability-relevant image state: this is a palette image (`im->trueColor == 0`) with no prior transparent entry yet (`im->transparent == -1`).

Because step 2 stored `Transparent = 0`, the GIF loader calls `gdImageColorTransparent(im, 0)` on the fresh palette image from steps 3-4. On the exact 28-byte witness, the file ends after the descriptor, but `ReadImage()` is void and does not block this call.

Root cause. The witnessed call reaches the palette-image path with `color == 0` and `im->trueColor == 0`, so the present guards all pass. The vulnerable code checks only the new `color` range and then immediately clears the previous transparent slot; it never checks whether `im->transparent` is still the sentinel `-1`.

Sink. With the current image state from step 4, this lvalue becomes `im->alpha[-1]`, an out-of-bounds write before the 256-entry palette alpha array. Stage 01 reproduces `runtime error: index -1 out of bounds for type 'int [256]'` at this exact statement.

cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch edits the exact crashing statement in `src/gd.c`, adding `if (im->transparent != -1)` before `im->alpha[im->transparent] = gdAlphaOpaque;`. Stage 02 did not perform fixed-version dynamic validation.

poc.trigger: Stage 01's saved vulnerable run executed `PYTHONPATH=gt_generation python3 -m gt_toolkit arvo-workspace --result-dir /mnt/datastore/gt_generation/gt_results/arvo_37687 run --version vulnerable --expect crash`, fed the staged `poc` to `/out/gif_target`, and reproduced `UndefinedBehaviorSanitizer: runtime error: index -1 out of bounds for type 'int [256]'` in `gdImageColorTransparent` with stack `gdImageColorTransparent -> gdImageCreateFromGifCtx -> gdImageCreateFromGifPtr`.

format.name: GIF89a with malformed 1-byte Graphic Control Extension
format.contract: The verified trigger is exactly the staged 28-byte witness `47 49 46 38 39 61 20 20 20 FF 20 20 20 21 F9 01 FF 00 2C 20 1E 20 20 20 00 20 00 20`. Its Graphic Control Extension bytes are `21 F9 01 FF 00`: the block-size byte `01` makes `GetDataBlock()` copy only one data byte `FF` into zeroed `buf[4]`, so `DoExtension()` sees the transparency flag set and stores `Transparent = buf[3] = 0`. The following image descriptor bytes `2C 20 1E 20 20 20 00 20 00 20` create a 32x32 palette frame, and the file then ends before the first LZW code-size byte. `gdImageCreateFromGifCtx()` nevertheless calls `gdImageColorTransparent(im, 0)` on the fresh image whose `im->transparent` sentinel is still `-1`. The trigger semantics recorded here do not generalize beyond this exact witness layout.
